entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
China Construction Bank Corporation (CCB), founded in Beijing in 1954 as the People's Construction Bank of China, is the world's second-largest bank by assets ($4.74 trillion) and China's primary lender for infrastructure and urban development — financing the Three Gorges Dam, the Beijing-Shanghai High Speed Railway, millions of housing units, and the Belt and Road Initiative's infrastructure loans across 60+ countries. CCB's transformation from a state construction treasury to a commercial bank (1994-2004) mirrors China's broader economic transformation.

CCB was founded to manage state funds for China's First Five Year Plan (1953-1957) capital construction — effectively functioning as a government treasury rather than a bank. The 1994 Chinese banking reform separated policy banking from commercial banking, converting CCB into a commercial entity. The 2005 IPO on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange raised $9.2 billion — the world's largest IPO at the time — with Bank of America acquiring a 9% strategic stake.

CCB's role in Chinese urbanization is structural: as China's population migrated from 20% urban (1980) to 65% urban (2023), CCB financed the apartment buildings, metro systems, highways, and commercial buildings that housed and connected 600 million new urban dwellers. The Belt and Road Initiative (since 2013) has made CCB a global infrastructure lender: CCB has financed ports, railways, power plants, and industrial parks across Africa, Asia, and Latin America — making it the world's most consequential development bank.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: China Construction Bank's role in financing China's urbanization — from 20% to 65% urban in 40 years, housing 600 million new city dwellers — and the Belt and Road Initiative's global infrastructure makes CCB the development bank whose lending has most immediately shaped 21st-century economic geography.
